cards.title: Earthquake indoors: Drop, Cover, and Hold On
facts: Falling debris, collapsing ceiling plaster, and shattering glass cause most earthquake injuries.
Taking shelter under sturdy furniture protects your vital head, neck, and torso.
do: DROP onto your hands and knees immediately to prevent being knocked over
COVER your head and neck under a sturdy table, desk, or bed
HOLD ON to the furniture leg until the ground stops shaking
dont: Never run outside during active shaking (falling building tiles and glass will strike you)
Never use elevators during or immediately after an earthquake

myths.statement: Standing in a doorway is the safest spot during an indoor earthquake.
myths.truth: Modern door frames are not reinforced and doors swinging violently crush fingers. Drop, cover, and hold under a desk.

quiz.q: What is the internationally proven emergency response when ground shaking starts indoors?
options: Drop, Cover, and Hold On under a sturdy desk
quiz.explanation: Dropping low under sturdy desks protects vital organs from falling masonry and glass.

situations: In the classroom or home at {at}, violent earthquake tremors begin rattling the room.
scenario.question: What should {name} do immediately?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Drop immediately under a sturdy desk or table
rubric.note: Prevents being thrown down and protects from ceiling debris.

rubric.point: Hold onto the desk legs and cover head and neck with arms
rubric.note: Keeps shield in place as furniture shifts.

rubric.point: Stay indoors away from windows until shaking ceases completely
rubric.note: Escaping mid-shake is when most injuries occur.
rubric.keys: stay indoors|away from windows|wait for shaking to stop

cards.title: Earthquake outdoors: Finding open space
facts: Outside buildings, the greatest hazards are falling glass facades, signage, brick cornices, and electric poles.
The 'danger zone' extends directly outwards from exterior building walls.
do: Move quickly to an open clearing away from buildings, streetlights, and power cables
Drop to the ground and cover your head until shaking stops
If in a vehicle, have the driver pull over safely away from overpasses and bridges
dont: Never shelter directly under building balconies, awnings, or billboards
Never touch fallen overhead electric cables

myths.statement: Standing right next to the outer wall of a tall building protects you during an earthquake.
myths.truth: Exterior walls shed glass, air conditioners, and concrete slabs first. Move into open clearings.

quiz.q: When an earthquake strikes while you are walking outdoors on a street, where should you head?
options: Into an open ground or wide space away from buildings and power poles
quiz.explanation: Open spaces away from falling overhead architecture are the safest outdoor refuge zones.

situations: Walking in a market street at {at}, the ground shakes violently and streetlamps sway.
scenario.question: How should {name} seek safety?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Move away from building walls, hoardings, and electric poles into an open area
rubric.keys: open space|away from buildings|clear area|no poles

rubric.point: Drop to the ground and protect your head with your bag or hands
Stay alert to moving vehicles and stay away from elevated flyovers

cards.title: Post-earthquake evacuation: Gas, aftershocks and stairs
facts: Earthquakes sever underground gas lines and weaken building support pillars.
Aftershocks can occur minutes, hours, or days later, collapsing already-damaged structures.
do: Evacuate using stairwells calmly once shaking stops; never use elevators
Check for gas leaks: if you smell gas, open windows, do not touch switches, and evacuate outside
Expect aftershocks and be prepared to Drop, Cover, and Hold on again
dont: Never light matches, candles, or lighters after an earthquake
Never re-enter a visibly cracked building until certified safe by structural engineers

myths.statement: Using the elevator right after an earthquake is safe if power is working.
myths.truth: Elevator shafts warp during quakes and aftershocks will trap you inside in total darkness. Take stairs.

quiz.q: Why must you never strike a match or lighter after an earthquake?
options: Broken underground gas pipes can cause an instant explosion
quiz.explanation: Gas leaks are widespread post-quake; any spark causes devastating fires.

situations: The ground stops shaking at {at}. {name}'s family needs to evacuate their multi-story building.
scenario.question: What evacuation protocol should {name} ensure?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Take the stairs calmly in single file; never use the elevator
rubric.note: Prevents getting trapped in damaged elevator shafts.

rubric.point: Do not switch on lights or strike matches in case of broken gas lines
Assemble at the outdoor neighborhood open ground and prepare for aftershocks

dangerous: light candle to see in dark

cards.title: Home flood evacuation: Moving high and cutting power
facts: Just 15 cm (6 inches) of fast-moving floodwater can knock a person off their feet.
Rising floodwaters reaching wall sockets electrocute entire flooded ground floors.
do: Switch off main electrical circuit breakers and close the cylinder gas regulator before evacuating
Move to upper floors or higher ground with your emergency go-bag
Follow official disaster warnings and evacuate early before water cuts off road exits
dont: Never walk, swim, or drive through moving floodwaters ('Turn Around, Don't Drown')
Never touch electrical equipment while standing in water

myths.statement: If floodwater looks only ankle-deep, it is completely safe to walk across the street.
myths.truth: Ankle-deep rushing water possesses enormous kinetic force and hides open manholes and live electrical cables.

quiz.q: What is the vital electrical action before water enters your home?
options: Turn off the main electrical circuit breaker (MCB) immediately
quiz.explanation: Cutting mains power prevents waterlogged house electrocution.

situations: Monsoon rains cause river water to rise rapidly near {name}'s home at {at}.
scenario.question: What should {name} and family do before water enters the ground floor?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Switch off the main electrical power breaker and turn off gas regulator
rubric.note: Eliminates electrocution and gas fire risks.

rubric.point: Move essential documents, medications, and family to higher floors or relief shelter
Do not wade through rushing brown floodwater outside
rubric.note: Prevents drowning and missing drain falls.

cards.title: Cyclone alert readiness: Securing home and tracking alerts
facts: Tropical cyclones produce destructive winds over 150 km/h, storm surges, and torrential downpours.
Unsecured tin roofs, loose metal sheets, and tree branches turn into deadly high-speed projectiles.
do: Secure or bring indoors all loose outdoor objects, flowerpots, and tin sheets
Tape large window panes diagonally with duct tape to prevent flying glass shards
Tune into official All India Radio / IMD weather bulletins on a battery-powered radio or phone
dont: Never step outside during the calm 'eye of the storm' (destructive reverse winds resume abruptly)
Never believe unverified WhatsApp cyclone forward rumors

myths.statement: When the wind suddenly goes completely calm during a cyclone, the storm is officially over.
myths.truth: This is the 'eye of the cyclone'. The other half of the eyewall with violent opposite winds will strike shortly.

quiz.q: What happens when the calm 'eye' of a tropical cyclone passes directly overhead?
options: Winds drop temporarily, but ferocious opposite-direction winds will strike within minutes
quiz.explanation: The eye is surrounded by the destructive eyewall; remain indoors.

situations: A Red Alert cyclone warning is issued for {name}'s coastal district at {at}.
scenario.question: How should {name} prepare the home?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Secure loose outdoor objects, metal sheets, and board or tape windows
rubric.note: Stops objects turning into lethal flying missiles.

rubric.point: Keep emergency drinking water, battery torches, and a radio ready
rubric.note: Essential for expected multi-day power outages.

rubric.point: Stay indoors in the strongest central room away from windows until all-clear is given
rubric.note: Protects from roof and window failures.

dangerous: go to the beach to see waves
step outside during the calm eye

cards.title: Lightning storm safety: The 30-30 rule and outdoor crouching
facts: A lightning bolt carries over 300 million volts of electricity and is hotter than the surface of the sun.
Tall solitary trees and open metal poles act as natural lightning rods; standing under them is lethal.
do: Follow the 30-30 Rule: If time between lightning flash and thunder is under 30 seconds, get indoors immediately
Stay inside a fully enclosed building or metal-roofed car until 30 minutes after the last thunderclap
If caught in an open field, crouch low on the balls of your feet with heels touching ('lightning crouch')
dont: Never shelter under isolated tall trees or tin-roofed sheds in open fields
Never lie flat on the wet ground (ground currents conduct through your whole body)

myths.statement: Standing under a tall solitary tree during a thunderstorm keeps you dry and safe.
myths.truth: Lightning hits the highest point; current blasts down the trunk and jumps to nearby people (side flash).

quiz.q: What is the safest body posture if caught in an open meadow with zero indoor shelter during lightning?
options: Crouch low on balls of feet, tuck head, with heels touching together
quiz.explanation: Crouching minimizes height and touching heels lets current loop through feet without crossing the heart.

situations: A sudden thunderstorm with frequent lightning strikes erupts while {name} is in a sports field at {at}.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Immediately seek shelter inside a sturdy building or closed vehicle
rubric.note: Safest Faraday cage and structural protection.

rubric.point: Do not shelter under isolated tall trees or touch metal fences
rubric.note: Eliminates side-flash and ground current paths.
rubric.keys: no tall trees|no metal fences|avoid poles

rubric.point: If trapped in the open, crouch low on balls of feet without lying flat

cards.title: Heatwave survival: Hydration, ORS and timing activities
facts: Heatstroke occurs when internal body temperature exceeds 40°C, causing brain and organ shutdown.
Drinking plain water alone is insufficient during heavy sweating; electrolytes (salts) must be replenished.
do: Drink plenty of water, ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts), lassi, chaas, and lemon water regularly
Schedule essential outdoor chores before 10 AM or after 5 PM, avoiding peak afternoon sun
Wear loose, light-colored cotton clothing and cover your head with a damp cloth or wide-brim hat
dont: Never leave children or pets locked inside parked cars (temperatures reach fatal 60°C in 15 mins)
Never do strenuous outdoor sports during afternoon red heat alert hours

myths.statement: You only need to drink water when you feel extremely thirsty during a heatwave.
myths.truth: Thirst is a delayed symptom; by the time you feel parched, your body is already clinically dehydrated.

quiz.q: What should you drink alongside water during severe 44°C summer heatwaves?
options: Electrolyte fluids like ORS, buttermilk (chaas), and lemon water with salt
quiz.explanation: Electrolytes replace sodium and potassium lost through sweat, preventing heat cramps and stroke.

situations: The thermometer reads 45°C during an official Heatwave Alert at {at}.
scenario.question: How should {name} structure their day?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stay indoors in shaded, ventilated spaces during peak hours (12 PM to 4 PM)
rubric.keys: stay indoors|avoid peak sun|12 to 4 pm|shade

rubric.point: Hydrate continuously with water, ORS, and homemade cooling drinks (aam panna, chaas)
Wear loose, breathable cotton clothes and cover head if stepping out
rubric.note: Prevents sunburn and solar heat absorption.

cards.title: Cold wave survival: Layering and carbon monoxide danger
facts: Burning coal angithis, charcoal braziers, or wood in closed bedrooms releases lethal Carbon Monoxide (CO).
Carbon Monoxide is an invisible, odorless, tasteless gas that silently suffocates sleeping families.
do: Wear multiple loose, warm layers (thermal inners, woolens, windbreaker) instead of one heavy coat
Ensure active cross-ventilation (leave windows slightly cracked) if using heating appliances
Cover head, neck, hands, and feet (warm cap, muffler, woolen socks) where body heat radiates fastest
dont: Never sleep in an airtight closed room with a burning coal angithi or unvented gas heater
Never ignore symptoms of hypothermia: uncontrollable shivering, slurred speech, and extreme drowsiness

myths.statement: Sleeping with a burning charcoal angithi in an airtight bedroom keeps the family warm and completely safe.
myths.truth: Airtight coal burning produces lethal carbon monoxide, causing hundreds of fatal winter asphyxiations yearly.

quiz.q: Why is it deadly to burn a coal angithi or wood brazier inside a tightly sealed bedroom with all windows closed?
options: Incomplete combustion generates invisible, odorless Carbon Monoxide gas that kills in sleep
quiz.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds to hemoglobin 200 times stronger than oxygen, causing painless suffocation.

situations: During freezing winter temperatures at {at}, relatives want to bring a glowing charcoal angithi into a closed bedroom.
scenario.question: What life-saving intervention must {name} make?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Explain that burning charcoal in an enclosed room generates lethal Carbon Monoxide gas
Insist on keeping windows cracked for fresh air ventilation if any heater is used
Use extra woolen blankets and multiple clothing layers for warmth instead of open coal

dangerous: seal all windows with burning coal

cards.title: Hillside landslides: Warning signs and safe evacuation
facts: Prolonged torrential monsoon rains saturate mountain soil, causing catastrophic mud and boulder slides.
Warning signs include tilted trees, cracks opening on slopes, jammed doors, and sudden muddy stream surges.
do: Evacuate immediately to designated ridge shelters if you observe widening soil cracks on hillside slopes
Stay alert during continuous heavy hill rainfall and listen for rumbling sounds like locomotives
Avoid building or camping near steep slopes, drainage ravines, and mountain stream channels
dont: Never stay in valley bottoms directly in the path of a potential mudflow
Never drive across road sections with falling rocks or fresh mudslides

myths.statement: Landslides strike instantly with zero prior warning signs on the hillside.
myths.truth: Landslides give multiple advance warnings: tilting telephone poles, new ground cracks, and muddy springs.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an early physical warning sign of an impending hillside landslide?
options: Trees and electric poles tilting sideways and new cracks appearing in masonry walls
quiz.explanation: Soil creep tilts rooted poles and trees days before complete slope failure.

situations: On a vacation or trip in a hilly region at {at}, continuous heavy rains cause new cracks to appear in the lodge's slope.
scenario.question: What should {name} and guests do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Alert adults and evacuate uphill to stable ridge ground away from the slope
rubric.note: Moves out of downward mud avalanche trajectory.

rubric.point: Listen for ominous deep rumbling sounds or sudden muddying of clear streams
Report slope movement to local administration and disaster helplines

dangerous: hide in basement at bottom of hill

sources.name: Geological Survey of India (GSI Landslide Division)

cards.title: Coastal tsunami warning signs: Sea withdrawal and high ground
facts: Undersea earthquakes displace massive water columns, generating tsunami wave trains over 800 km/h.
Nature's primary visual tsunami warning is a dramatic, sudden retreat of ocean water exposing the seabed.
do: If you feel a strong coastal earthquake or see the sea suddenly pull back, run inland and uphill immediately
Climb to elevated ground at least 30 meters above sea level, or to the 4th floor of a reinforced concrete building
Stay on high ground for several hours: tsunamis arrive as a series of multiple waves over hours
dont: Never run down to the beach to collect stranded fish or look at the exposed seabed
Never wait for an official siren if natural warning signs (quake, sea retreat) occur

myths.statement: A tsunami is just one big wave; once the first wave recedes, it is safe to return to the beach.
myths.truth: Tsunamis are a series of wave crests; the second or third wave is frequently much larger than the first.

quiz.q: You are on a beach when the ocean water suddenly pulls back hundreds of meters, exposing stranded shells. What do you do?
options: Run out onto the wet sand to collect shells
Turn around immediately and sprint inland to high ground
quiz.explanation: Sudden sea withdrawal is the definitive sign of a massive incoming tsunami wave crest. Run inland.

situations: While visiting a coastal beach at {at}, {name} notices the ocean water pulling back rapidly into the horizon.
scenario.question: What urgent action must {name} initiate?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Shout to companions and run inland toward high ground immediately
rubric.keys: run inland|high ground|sprint away from beach

rubric.point: Do not pause to collect belongings, take videos, or gather stranded marine life
Remain on elevated ground for hours until disaster authorities issue official all-clear

dangerous: wait for official announcement on beach

sources.name: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)

cards.title: Assembling a family Emergency Go-Bag (72-hour survival kit)
facts: During major disasters, municipal electricity, tap water, and cellular networks can stay down for 72 hours.
A pre-packed, waterproof Go-Bag ensures your family can evacuate in under 60 seconds.
do: Pack essential documents (Aadhaar, property papers, insurance) sealed inside waterproof plastic ziplocks
Include battery torches, spare batteries, a loud emergency whistle, and a portable battery power bank
Pack water bottles, water purification tablets, dry non-perishable rations (chana, biscuits), and a first aid kit
dont: Never overload the Go-Bag so heavily that a student cannot easily carry it while running
Never forget critical daily prescription medicines required by family elders

myths.statement: A disaster Emergency Go-Bag is only needed in movies and war zones.
myths.truth: Floods, earthquakes, and cyclones strike Indian cities with zero warning; a Go-Bag saves lives every year.

quiz.q: What is the most critical item to keep inside waterproof bags within your emergency kit?
options: Vital personal identification documents, medical papers, and emergency contact list
quiz.explanation: Waterproof document storage protects legal identity and allows rapid post-disaster insurance and relief.

situations: {name}'s family at {at} is preparing their 72-hour disaster Emergency Go-Bag.
scenario.question: What core items should {name} ensure are packed inside?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Store key family documents and emergency cash in sealed waterproof pouches
rubric.note: Protects vital identity and emergency finances.

rubric.point: Pack a battery-powered torch, emergency whistle, and portable phone power bank
Include dry ready-to-eat food, water purification tablets, and basic first aid

cards.title: Family disaster communication plan: Emergency contacts and meeting spots
facts: Local mobile cell towers crash during disasters due to power cuts and massive calling congestion.
Out-of-state long-distance SMS text messages frequently pass through when local voice calls fail.
do: Designate an out-of-city relative (Aunt/Uncle in another state) as the central family check-in contact
Memorize your parents' mobile phone numbers by heart rather than relying on phone memory
Agree on two fixed family meeting points: one right outside your home, and one outside the neighborhood
dont: Never clog emergency networks with continuous long phone calls; send short SMS check-in texts
Never leave an agreed evacuation meeting point without leaving a written note

myths.statement: In a major earthquake, you will easily be able to video call your parents on mobile phones.
myths.truth: Local cellular towers fail instantly during major disasters. Plan offline meeting spots and out-of-state SMS.

quiz.q: Why should your family designate an out-of-state relative as your emergency disaster check-in contact?
options: Local city lines get jam-packed, while long-distance text routing through other states stays operational
quiz.explanation: An out-of-area contact acts as a central communication bridge when local networks fail.

situations: Planning family disaster readiness at {at}, {name} discusses emergency communication.
scenario.question: What key plan should {name} establish?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Memorize two primary parent phone numbers and designate an out-of-state family contact
rubric.note: Ensures communication when local lines fail.
rubric.keys: memorize phone numbers|out of town contact|central contact

rubric.point: Agree on two specific physical meeting spots (one local, one outside neighborhood)
Use short SMS text messages instead of continuous voice calls during network congestion

cards.title: Official disaster alerts vs viral WhatsApp panic rumors
facts: Viral social media forwards spread fabricated dam-burst warnings, false death tolls, and fake dates.
The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and IMD publish verified color-coded alerts (Yellow, Orange, Red).
do: Rely exclusively on verified government sources: NDMA (sachet.ndma.gov.in), IMD, and District Collector handles
Check the 'Sachet' National Disaster Alert Portal app on your smartphone for localized warnings
Verify sensational forward claims against official press releases before forwarding to family groups
dont: Never forward unverified voice notes claiming 'a massive dam has collapsed' or 'super-cyclone incoming'
Never share outdated disaster photos from previous years as current news

myths.statement: Forwarding every alarming disaster audio clip on WhatsApp helps warn your family just in case.
myths.truth: Panic rumors cause stampedes, choke emergency helplines, and prevent real relief from reaching victims.

quiz.q: What is the official disaster early warning portal and mobile app developed by NDMA India?
quiz.explanation: SACHET is the Government of India's integrated early warning platform providing real-time regional alerts.

situations: A scary audio clip spreads on family WhatsApp at {at} claiming an earthquake will strike the city at 4 PM.
scenario.question: How should {name} debunk this panic rumor?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Explain that science CANNOT predict exact earthquake times; the forward is a fabricated hoax
Cross-check alerts on the official NDMA SACHET portal or IMD official handles
Ask family members to delete the forward and not share panic in society groups
rubric.note: Stops the viral chain of panic.

cards.title: Dilapidated walls and old building collapses in monsoon
facts: Heavy monsoon rains saturate lime mortar and soil foundations, causing sudden boundary wall collapses.
Over 60% of monsoon structural fatalities occur when pedestrians walk beside waterlogged old walls.
do: Walk in the center of lanes, keeping a wide 3-meter safety margin away from old boundary walls
Avoid taking shelter from rain under decaying concrete awnings, balconies, or leaning brick fences
Report dangerously tilted or water-seeping walls to your local municipal ward office
dont: Never lean your bicycle or stand directly against waterlogged masonry walls during downpours
Never ignore fresh cracks or bulging in boundary walls

myths.statement: Standing right under a cracked building balcony keeps you dry from monsoon rain safely.
myths.truth: Waterlogged concrete balconies collapse without warning under the weight of accumulated rainwater.

quiz.q: Why is it dangerous to walk right beside ancient boundary walls during heavy monsoon rain?
options: Saturated rainwater destabilizes old foundations, causing sudden wall collapses onto pedestrians
quiz.explanation: Water absorption weakens mortar bonds, causing heavy masonry walls to topple outward.

situations: Walking home in torrential rain at {at}, {name} sees classmates sheltering under an ancient crumbling boundary wall.
scenario.question: What should {name} urgently advise?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Move away from the wall and maintain a wide standoff safety distance
rubric.note: Prevents being crushed by sudden structural failure.
rubric.keys: move away from wall|keep distance|standoff distance

rubric.point: Explain that waterlogged brick foundations can collapse outward with zero warning
Seek shelter inside a sturdy, modern shop or permanent concrete structure

sources.name: Building Materials and Technology Promotion Council (BMTPC)

cards.title: Submerged electric wires and step potential in floodwaters
facts: Fallen live overhead power lines electrify surrounding pooled water for dozens of meters.
'Step potential' occurs when voltage differences between your two feet create a lethal shock loop.
do: Treat all standing rainwater around electric poles, transformers, or fallen wires as live and lethal
If you feel a tingling sensation in your feet while walking, stop immediately, keep feet together, and bunny-hop away
Alert local electricity distribution officials and police immediately to shut off power to the sector
dont: Never walk or cycle through pooled water near leaning electric poles or dangling cables
Never touch metal gates, lampposts, or signboards submerged in water

myths.statement: Waterlogged puddles around electric transformers are harmless unless you touch the metal pole directly.
myths.truth: Current leaks directly into pooled water, creating lethal electrical gradients across the surface.

quiz.q: What should you do if your legs feel a sudden electric tingling sensation in shallow floodwater?
options: Keep feet tightly together and bunny-hop or shuffle away without lifting feet apart
quiz.explanation: Keeping feet together eliminates the voltage difference ('step potential') across your body.

situations: After a severe storm at {at}, a heavy tree branch has snapped a high-voltage wire into a large water puddle.
scenario.question: How should {name} react?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stay at least 15 meters away and do not step into the waterlogged area
rubric.keys: stay away|15 meters|don'?t step in water|live wire

rubric.point: Warn other pedestrians and cyclists loudly to stay back
Call the electricity emergency complaint number and police 112 immediately
rubric.note: Ensures grid technicians de-energize the feeder.

dangerous: touch the wire with a stick

sources.name: Central Electricity Authority (Measures Relating to Safety)

cards.title: Safe drinking water after floods: Boiling and chlorine tablets
facts: Floodwaters submerge municipal pipelines, mixing sewage, animal carcasses, and cholera bacteria into drinking wells.
Consuming unpurified floodwater triggers deadly epidemics of cholera, typhoid, and hepatitis A.
do: Boil all drinking water vigorously at a rolling boil for at least 1 to 3 continuous minutes
Use Halazone / chlorine water purification tablets according to packaging instructions if boiling is impossible
Store purified drinking water in narrow-mouthed, clean containers with secure lids
dont: Never drink clear-looking tap water after a flood without boiling (pathogens are invisible)
Never wash dishes, fruit, or brush teeth with contaminated floodwater

myths.statement: If floodwater from a well looks crystal clear, it is completely pure and safe to drink without boiling.
myths.truth: Deadly pathogens like cholera and typhoid bacteria are microscopic and thrive in clear-looking water.

quiz.q: How long must drinking water be kept at a vigorous rolling boil to sterilize post-flood water?
options: At least 1 to 3 minutes of continuous rolling boiling
quiz.explanation: 1-3 minutes of vigorous rolling boiling kills all vegetative bacteria, viruses, and amoebic cysts.

situations: Following heavy river floods at {at}, the municipal tap water runs with a strange smell.
scenario.question: What water purification protocol must {name} implement at home?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Bring all drinking water to a continuous rolling boil for at least 1-3 minutes
Use chlorine disinfection tablets if gas or electricity for boiling is unavailable
Keep purified water covered in clean containers; do not drink raw tap water

sources.name: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality in Emergencies

cards.title: Community solidarity: Assisting elderly and disabled neighbors
facts: Elderly citizens, persons with mobility challenges, and toddlers face severe evacuation barriers.
A resilient community checks on vulnerable households within the first 15 minutes of a disaster alert.
do: Check on elderly or disabled neighbors during evacuation alerts to ensure they have heard the warning
Help carry essential medications, walking canes, and emergency bags for senior citizens
Assist them along safe evacuation routes calmly without rushing or creating panic
dont: Never leave elderly neighbors behind in ground-floor flood zones without verification
Never shout or cause hysteria that triggers cardiac distress in vulnerable seniors

myths.statement: During disaster evacuation, you should only care about yourself and ignore elderly neighbors.
myths.truth: Community mutual aid is what saves lives during disasters before government rescue boats arrive.

quiz.q: What is the most compassionate civic action during a neighborhood evacuation warning?
options: Knock on elderly or disabled neighbors' doors to ensure they know and offer evacuation help
quiz.explanation: Checking on vulnerable neighbors ensures nobody is left trapped in flood or fire zones.

situations: A cyclone or flood evacuation alert sounds in the neighborhood at {at}.
scenario.question: How should {name} demonstrate community leadership?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Check on elderly or disabled neighbors living nearby to confirm they are evacuating safely
rubric.note: Ensures vulnerable individuals are accounted for.
rubric.keys: check on elderly|assist neighbors|disabled neighbors|evacuation help

rubric.point: Help them pack vital prescription medicines, walking aids, and identity cards
Guide them calmly to the community relief center or high-ground assembly point

sources.name: NDMA Community Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM)

cards.title: School disaster evacuation drills: Discipline beats panic
facts: Historical disaster analyses show that stairwell stampedes cause 4 times more injuries than building damage.
Regular disaster drills build muscle memory, allowing students to evacuate calmly on instinct.
do: Take school disaster drills seriously as realistic life-saving training, not playtime
Follow teacher directions instantly, walk briskly in single file, and maintain total silence
Keep hands free: do not hold hands across the staircase or stop to pick up dropped pens
dont: Never run, push, scream, or shove on school staircases during an evacuation drill
Never joke or make false alarm screams that trigger panic stampedes

myths.statement: School disaster drills are boring wastes of class time that will never be used in real life.
myths.truth: Schools that practice regular drills achieve 100% casualty-free evacuations during real earthquakes and fires.

quiz.q: What is the single most critical behavioral rule when evacuating school staircases during a drill?
options: Run as fast as you can
Walk calmly in single file, no pushing, no running, and maintain silence
quiz.explanation: Orderly walking in single file prevents deadly crowd crushes and tripping on stairwells.

situations: A disaster evacuation siren rings across the school campus at {at}.
scenario.question: How should {name} and classmates conduct themselves?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Walk briskly in orderly single file without running or pushing
Maintain silence so teachers' emergency instructions can be heard by all
Assemble at the designated outdoor school sports ground for roll-call headcount
rubric.note: Verifies all students are safely accounted for.

dangerous: stop to tie shoelaces on stairs
